answer: Every new identity enters fourteen-epoch maturation in an ivory ledger: its 80-credit stake locks, it holds zero weight and earns nothing until the period ends. The kth fake identity locks its own 80 credits for the full period, so 1,000 fakes tie up 80,000 credits earning zero, with no stake reuse. A violet flag marks borrowed work history, freezing the stake for inspection. Each identity is a vertex in the ledger, and shared funding edges expose the cluster. A rented-history dodge fails because one record cannot mature twice; an honest agent waits once, keeping full weight.
